title: Neighborhood sound booth
passage: Thanks for coming to the neighborhood sound booth. People sometimes arrive with a whole story in mind, but our display plays just a short clip at a time. Start with the sound you remember, rather than telling us when and where it happened. You can add those details on a card after you record. If you bring an object that makes that sound, try it once before we start. The volunteer will move the microphone if the sound is too faint. Before you leave, listen to your clip with headphones. The booth speaker is off so it won’t play while someone else is recording.
passageZh: 感謝各位來到社區聲音採集亭。有些人帶著一整個故事來，但展示每次只播一小段錄音。請先從記得的聲音開始，不用先交代事情何時、在哪裡發生。錄完後，可以把那些細節補在卡上。如果你帶了能發出該聲音的物品，請在開始錄音前先試一次。聲音太微弱時，志工會移動麥克風。離開前請用耳機試聽自己的音檔。錄音亭喇叭會關著，以免別人錄音時播放聲音。

formalSourcePlan.rangeCue: Questions 92 through 94 refer to the following talk.
standaloneStems: Number 92. What should a visitor do with a remembered sound and the details of where it happened?
Number 93. How can the volunteer help if an object makes a sound that is too quiet?
Number 94. Why is the booth speaker turned off?
